summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style entry on Dehradun, also called Dehra Dun, the interim capital of the Indian state of Uttarakhand. It places the city in the Garhwal region, gives its distances from New Delhi and Chandigarh, and notes its role as a Counter Magnet of the National Capital Region. It also mentions the town's earlier official name, Dehra, used during the British Raj.
one_line: Dehradun is the interim capital of Uttarakhand, India, in the Garhwal region, and a Counter Magnet of the National Capital Region.
key_facts: Dehradun, also spelled Dehra Dun, is the interim capital city of Uttarakhand, a state in the northern part of India.
Dehradun is located in the Garhwal region.
Dehradun lies 236 kilometres (147 mi) north of India's capital New Delhi.
Dehradun is 168 kilometres (104 mi) from Chandigarh.
Dehradun is one of the Counter Magnets of the National Capital Region (NCR).
The NCR Counter Magnet program is being developed as an alternative centre of growth to help ease migration and population explosion in the Delhi metropolitan area.
Dehradun is being developed to establish a smart city.
During the days of the British Raj, the official name of the town was Dehra.
